audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rated all seven stages 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet both read Aurora for levels 1-5 and Anivia from 6. Two different answers on the same page.
audit.why: The content layer is the one that matches the kits: Anivia has no dash and her only pre-6 threat is a slow-moving 1075-range sphere on 11s at rank 1, so an Aurora with a hop picks every early trade. Glacial Storm at 6 changes who owns the ground.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side moved to Aurora at 4/10, phases[4..6].side to Anivia at 6/10, with each why rewritten in the same proposal to argue the verdict above it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and late spikes were argued through 'Between Worlds' phase doesn't deal damage' and 'only delays the inevitable' — Aurora's R has no phase at all, and neither line named what actually changes at 6.
audit.why: What changes at 6 is Frostbite: Riot's text says its damage is DOUBLED if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm. Frostbite is a flat 4s cooldown, so time spent standing in the storm is time taking doubled hits.
audit.corrected: 6 is Glacial Storm doubling a 4-second Frostbite. Late is Crystallize: a 1000-range impassable wall on a flat 17s that can cut the leap you were counting on.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit E/R/W text and cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions that decide this lane appear nowhere on the page. (a) Rebirth — Riot's text: upon taking fatal damage Anivia reverts to an egg and is reborn with full health. The word 'egg' does not occur once in the matchup. (b) Crystallize is an impassable wall that blocks all movement, and Aurora's W and R are both flagged as mobility that walls deny. The page also claimed sidestepping Flash Frost means 'her E never doubles', which is only half true — a fully formed Glacial Storm doubles Frostbite as well.
audit.why: Killing Anivia takes two health bars, and the wall is the thing that turns Aurora's exit into a trap. Both are load-bearing and both were absent.
audit.corrected: Break the egg or the kill did not happen. Do not spend Across the Veil while Crystallize (flat 17s, 1000 range) is up. Frostbite doubles off either Flash Frost or a formed storm.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit P/W/E text, ownerKit W/R dash flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit — it said 'count it out loud' instead of naming the count. dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' for an ability that is 11/10/9/8/7.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 3, plus a magnitude with no source.
audit.corrected: Flash Frost 11s at rank 1 and 7s at rank 5, Crystallize a flat 17s, Frostbite a flat 4s, Across the Veil 22s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twin Drift' is not an Aurora ability (spikes[0].text, early). spikes[2] also credits Aurora with 'early DoT output' and mid calls Frostbite an 'execute' — Riot's text gives Frostbite a damage doubler, not a threshold.
audit.why: Fabricated names and a fabricated mechanic; a player who plays around an execute plays the health bar wrong.
audit.corrected: The leap is Across the Veil (W). Frostbite doubles, it does not execute.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief ownerKit W text, enemyKit E text)

notes:
Level chart: the full layer read Skill on all seven rows while content and packet.levelChart both read Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Anivia/Anivia/Anivia. Content and packet agree with each other and with the kits, so I moved the full layer onto them rather than the other way round — side, rating and why proposed together for each row, and the content win[] rows were already correct so they were left untouched.

Derived-flag note: Anivia's Q carries hardCC, slow and zone flags; Riot's text supports the stun and the chill, so I wrote the stun. Her R flags say slow and zone, which matches. No flag looked like a misfire in this kit.

SuspectNames: 'Flash Frost's' and 'Glacial Storm's' are both real names with a possessive attached — false positives. Both lines were still edited for other reasons (a fabricated 'Twin Drift', and a missing statement of what the storm actually does).

Unverified and left alone: whether Crystallize can block Aurora's R leap or the teleport across her own zone. Both of Aurora's mobility spells carry the 'walls can deny' flag, so I said the wall ends the W leap — which the flag and the wall's 'blocks all movement' text jointly support — but I did not claim anything about the R teleport, which is a different mechanic and is not covered by either file.
